# Optimize the RFE-creator skill pipeline

## THE READER (who consumes what you edit)
At runtime these capabilities are read by `aws/claude-haiku-4-5` — capability tier: **mid**. The reader is a mid-capability model (e.g. ~100B open weights). Be EXPLICIT: imperative step-by-step rules, at least one worked few-shot example per non-trivial behavior, short decision chains, and literal argument/slot-filling docs on every tool parameter. Lean HARD on deterministic tool-code enforcement — a behavioral rule it 'knows' but skips must be enforced in code, not restated in prose.
Optimize your edits for THIS reader's capability level, not for your own. When the reader is weaker than you, prefer explicit rules, worked examples, and code enforcement over terse prose you would personally infer.


Focus: every failing task on the val split. Current val reward 0.897: 0 solid / 25 flaky / 0 failing of 25 tasks.



GOAL: raise the eval score THIS iteration, then STOP (the harness re-scores you — don't
run evaluation yourself). The capability is 7 independent Claude Code Agent Skills
(rfe.speedrun, rfe.create, rfe.auto-fix, rfe.review, rfe-feasibility-review, rfe.split,
rfe.submit) that together turn a problem statement into a reviewed, right-sized RFE
(Jira Feature Request). You may edit each skill's `SKILL.md` and its bundled
`prompts/*.md` / `*-template.md` files. Nothing else is yours to touch.

The eval's reward is a weighted mix of `rfe_quality` and `revision_quality` (LLM judges,
1-5 — the headroom is here) plus 8 boolean structural/consistency checks that currently
PASS (files_exist, frontmatter_valid, run_report_exists, recommendation_consistency,
revision_flag_consistency, pipeline_flow, architecture_context_used, revision_coverage).
**Never trade a passing boolean check for a quality gain** — a regressed boolean is a
much bigger loss than any quality-score improvement.

## Non-negotiable contracts (breaking these fails the run structurally, not just a score)
- **No HOW.** An RFE describes a business need (WHAT/WHY) — never implementation
  ("must use X", specific APIs/algorithms). Platform vocabulary from the input is fine;
  prescribing a solution is not. This is the #1 `rfe_quality` criterion.
- **Frontmatter contract.** Review files must keep `rfe_id, score, pass, recommendation,
  feasibility, auto_revised, scores.{what,why,open_to_how,not_a_task,right_sized}` —
  `frontmatter_valid` and `recommendation_consistency` parse these VERBATIM.
- **Revision evidence.** When a revision happens, leave the trail the judges look for
  (`before_score != score`, a non-empty Revision History section, `auto_revised: true`)
  — `revision_flag_consistency` and `revision_coverage` read only these artifacts.
- **skillsaw byte budget.** Each skill's `SKILL.md` is checked against
  `rfe-creator/.skillsaw.yaml` (warn 4000B, error 8000B). `rfe.review` (13282B) and
  `rfe.speedrun` (9534B) are ALREADY over the error budget in the seed — for these two,
  net byte count should go DOWN, not up; trim redundant prose before adding a rule.
  Check `rfe-skill-pipeline`'s `validate()` output (in `./guidance/`) before finalizing.

## The THREE TESTS every edit must pass
1. **REAL** — targets a cluster actually failing/low-scoring in `./trajectories/` this
   iteration (a low `rfe_quality`/`revision_quality` score, or a broken boolean check).
2. **SAFE** — does not change output on a currently-passing/well-scored case. A prose
   edit to `rfe.create`/`rfe.review` changes ALL future RFEs it touches, not just the
   failing one — check it against a passing case's expected shape before keeping it.
3. **VERIFIED** — re-read the edited section and confirm it says what you intended,
   still fits the budget, and did not remove a frontmatter field or Revision History
   mechanic a judge depends on.

## Read these first
- `./guidance/rfe-skill-pipeline/SKILL.md` — what's editable and the budget rule.
- `./guidance/diagnose/SKILL.md` — the failure-clustering method.
- `./trajectories/` — full traces (rfe-tasks/, rfe-reviews/, rfe-originals/ per case).
- `./LEDGER.md` / `./JOURNAL.md` / `./RUNMAP.md` — prior iterations' outcomes; don't
  re-try a change a RESULT line already shows regressed a passing case.


## Process (then STOP)
Parallelism: Your agent supports parallel subagents/worktrees (see ./guidance/optimizer/claude-code.md). FAN OUT to cover MANY clusters at once: one read-only subagent per trajectory-group to diagnose, then one edit-subagent per issue (each in its own worktree), then MERGE every edit into this ONE candidate with no conflicts. This is how a single iteration fixes many issues across many trajectories, not just the biggest one.
1. Diagnose `./trajectories/` — cluster low-scoring cases by shared root cause (vague
   business need, weak justification, prescriptive language, miscalibrated rubric
   scores, a broken boolean check).
2. For each cluster, edit the ONE skill whose SKILL.md governs it. Run the three tests.
3. Fill `PROCESS.md` (cluster -> edit -> verify line) and append your `JOURNAL.md` entry.

## What you are editing (the allowed edit space)
The capability under optimization is composed of these editable artifact(s). Use the FULL edit space below — do not limit yourself to trivial wording tweaks.
- **rfe-skill-pipeline** — Optimize the RFE-creation pipeline — 7 independent Claude Code Agent Skill packages (rfe.speedrun, rfe.create, rfe.auto-fix, rfe.review, rfe-feasibility-review, rfe.split, rfe.submit) that together create/review/auto-fix/split/submit RFEs.
  - Full guidance (read it): ./guidance/rfe-skill-pipeline/SKILL.md
## How your edit is judged
Algorithm: hill-climb:all. Your edited candidate is re-scored on the SAME held-out val tasks and compared to the current best (val reward 0.897). It is ACCEPTED only if the per-task improvement clears a significance bar (a noise margin), so a tiny or lucky change is rejected. Aim for a real, generalizing gain across a CLASS of failures — not a one-off patch to a single task (that overfits and gets rejected or hurts the held-out test).


## Run budget (iteration 2/10 (8 after this one); 1/10 consecutive rejects)

## Cross-iteration files in THIS working dir (clean ownership — read all)
- `LEDGER.md` — FACTS (framework, read-only): every iteration's outcome + the tasks it MEASURABLY broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was under 2·SE and so resolves nothing. Never re-introduce a change that broke a task; never redesign an edit because a task landed in `unresolved`.
- `JOURNAL.md` — HANDOVER (yours, append-only across the whole run): read the whole thing, then APPEND your entry for this iteration below the marker line. Do NOT edit earlier entries. This is how you avoid repeating refuted ideas and hitting the same plateau.
- `PROCESS.md` — EXPLAINABILITY (yours, REQUIRED this iteration): fill it in as you work (ranked issues, every edit + class, verify-the-fix, subagents/features used, what to preserve, what you skipped). It is snapshotted with your candidate.
- `RUNMAP.md` + `./prior_iterations/<id>/` — every prior iteration's PROCESS.md + capability diff, copied in for you. Read the ones targeting your cluster BEFORE proposing, so you build on prior work instead of repeating it.
- `INSIGHTS.md` — SUMMARIZED, VERIFIED findings (yours, append-only, optional most iterations): a distilled 'what worked / what didn't / what's promising' a future iteration reads INSTEAD of the whole journal. Add an entry whenever you have a new CONFIRMED finding (cite the RESULT that confirmed it).
- `META_INSIGHTS.md` — about the SEARCH PROCESS itself (yours, append-only): which strategies helped or stalled, what to try next. Update AT LEAST once, at the end of the run.
- `FRAMEWORK_IMPROVEMENTS.md` — cross-run suggestions for cap-evolve ITSELF, not this task (yours, append-only, optional): what confused you or was missing about the framework. Update AT LEAST once, at the end of the run.
- `.capevolve/run_20260909_092628/rejected.jsonl` — ALREADY-REFUTED approaches (framework, read-only; JSON lines, one per rejected candidate with the gate's reason). Read it and make each proposal STRUCTURALLY different from what is in it. Its sibling `history.jsonl` is the same record for accepts.
